applies_to: Network Thermostat RP32H (IP-WiFi) programmable thermostats with humidity control, connected over Ethernet to the NT-BAS ProtoNode FPC-N34 gateway.
summary: The NT-BAS ProtoNode reads a Network Thermostat RP32H over Ethernet and presents it as a BACnet MS/TP or BACnet IP device (Modbus, Metasys N2 and LonWorks are also offered). Each thermostat gets its own device instance. The profile exposes mode, fan and setpoint commands, temperatures, stage and override status, clock and vacation settings and the full 7-day, 4-period schedule. The H version adds humidify/dehumidify settings.
notes: From Appendix B.2, RP32H (IP-WIFI) mappings (guide pages 44-52).
The table gives no units, states or read/write column. Access here follows the Metasys N2 data type printed beside each object: AO/DO points are treated as writable, AI/DI as read-only.
Schedule objects repeat for each day (Monday-Sunday) and schedule period 1-4.
Lon Name and Lon SNVT columns are printed as TBD in this revision.

source.title: Network Thermostat's ProtoNode Startup Guide (ProtoNode FPC-N34 and FPC-N35, NT-BAS)

integration.summary: Write the system mode, fan mode and cooling/heating setpoints, and read the indoor temperature, heat/cool status, stage and override status. The thermostat also carries its own schedule, which the BMS can read or rewrite.

minimum_points.name: Outdoor_Temp
minimum_points.why: Outdoor temperature (if a sensor is fitted)

setup: Add each thermostat in the ProtoNode Web Configurator by picking its profile and entering the thermostat IP address, IP port, user name, password and the BACnet device instance (1-4,194,303).
ProtoNode DIP switches: S bank selects the field protocol, A bank sets the BACnet MS/TP MAC address, B bank sets the MS/TP baud rate.
The ProtoNode's own Ethernet port defaults to 192.168.1.24 (subnet 255.255.255.0); change it in the Web Configurator for BACnet IP.
gotchas: The guide gives no value codes for the Mode, Fan and other multi-state objects; read the State_Text from the device.
Schedule and vacation objects are stored in the thermostat; avoid cyclic writes.
